newsitem.title: USA: BP gets U.S. OK to drill Beaufort prospect.
newsitem.headline: BP gets U.S. OK to drill Beaufort prospect.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service said Tuesday it has approved an exploration plan for the Liberty prospect offshore in Alaska's Beaufort Sea.
The MMS granted permission to developer BP Exploration (Alaska) Inc., a unit of British Petroleum, to pursue its plan to evaluate the site.
BP acquired the prospect, located near Prudhoe Bay and about six miles east of the Endicott oil field, in an outercontinental shelf lease sale held September 18.
BP plans to construct an ice island using the remains of a gravel island built in the early 1980s, when Shell was exploring the site, then known as the Tern prospect, MMS said.
Construction of the island and associated ice roads was expected to start this month, with drilling expected to start around February 1, MMS said.
The plan still requires approval from the state for consistency with the Alaska coastal zone management plan, MMS said.
